summary_paragraph: An elderly female with a history of chronic diastolic heart failure, recurrent venous thromboembolism on warfarin, chronic chest and abdominal pain, and mild dementia was admitted for abdominal pain, poor oral intake, and diarrhea. Initial concern for constipation was revised when her son reported diarrhea, prompting stool testing that confirmed C. difficile infection. She was treated with intravenous fluids, potassium repletion, and oral metronidazole. Her abdominal pain improved, and elevated lactate resolved with hydration. Chronic chest pain remained stable and was not further investigated. Her INR rose during admission, likely due to illness and antibiotics, so warfarin was held at discharge with instructions to check INR the next day. Torsemide was held due to a dry clinical picture, with plans to restart after outpatient follow-up. She was discharged home in stable condition with a 14-day course of antibiotics, iron supplementation, and clear instructions for anticoagulation and heart failure medication management.
problems: Intestinal infection due to Clostridium difficile
Personal history of venous thrombosis and embolism
Diverticulosis of colon (without mention of hemorrhage)
Anticoagulants causing adverse effects in therapeutic use
